text: grep -n 'fn synthesized_error_omits_the_location_and_still_exits_255' -A 30 tests/uncaught_exception_report_tests.rs: 255), 258- "both uncaught paths must leave the same exit status" 259- ); 260- let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir); 261-} 262- 263-/// An exception that IS caught prints nothing and exits cleanly — the report is uncaught-only. 264-/// 265-/// Verifies buffered output SURVIVES an uncaught exception, and precedes the report. 266-/// 267-/// This helper used to write its message and exit without draining `ob_*` buffers, so 268-/// `ob_start(); echo "x"; throw …` printed NOTHING of the program's own output — the bytes were 269-/// simply dropped on the way out. PHP flushes the buffer first, then reports, so the program's 270-/// output comes first and the report follows. 271-/// 272-/// The order is what this asserts, not merely the presence of both: reporting before flushing 273-/// would still show every byte, in the wrong sequence, and a `contains` check could not tell the 274-/// difference.
